subject: Civil Engineering
title: Detention and Retention Basins
description: One-minute skill: Detention and Retention Basins.

hook.text: That empty pond behind the shopping mall isn't decorative — it catches floodwater.

buildup.text: Detention basins store runoff temporarily and release it slowly through a small outlet.

discovery.text: They reduce the peak flow downstream — spreading a sharp spike into a gentle curve.

twist.text: Retention basins keep a permanent pool — they also treat runoff by settling sediment.

climax.text: Most cities require new developments to include stormwater detention — zero net runoff increase.

punchline.text: Hold the water, slow it down, and the flood never reaches downtown.

quiz.question: How do detention basins reduce downstream flooding?
options: They permanently remove water from the watershed through evaporation
They store runoff temporarily and release it slowly, reducing peak flow
They redirect stormwater to a different watershed entirely

details.summary: Detention basins temporarily store stormwater and release it slowly through a restricted outlet, controlling peak flow rates. Retention basins permanently hold water, functioning as ponds that manage volume through infiltration and evaporation.
details.whyItMatters: Development increases peak runoff rates by 2-5 times pre-development levels. Without detention, downstream flooding and channel erosion worsen with every new development. Basins restore pre-development flow patterns.
takeaways: Detention basins empty between storms, controlling peak flow rate only
Retention basins maintain a permanent pool, also reducing total runoff volume
Multi-stage outlets control flows for multiple storm return periods simultaneously

faq.question: What is the difference between detention and retention in stormwater management?
faq.answer: Detention basins are dry between storms, temporarily storing water during events and draining through a restricted outlet within 24-72 hours. Retention basins maintain a permanent pool of water, functioning as constructed ponds.

faq.question: How do engineers size detention basins for new developments?
faq.answer: Engineers model the difference between post-development peak flow and the allowable release rate, sizing storage volume to hold the excess. Routing calculations determine the required volume and outlet configuration to match pre-development peak flows for multiple design storms.
